newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hungary asks Germany to take back hazardous waste.
newsitem.headline: Hungary asks Germany to take back hazardous waste.

text.p: Hungary has asked Germany to take back 380 tonnes of industrial chemicals which Hungarian authorities suspect is an illegal consignment of hazardous waste, according to Bonn's environment ministry.
The Bonn ministry said on Saturday that the matter was now the responsibility of the state environment ministry in Lower Saxony.

But a Lower Saxony spokeswoman said it was not clear why her state should be responsible. She also said it was by no means certain that the chemicals in question were hazardous waste rather than materials legitimately destined for reprocessing.
The news weekly Der Spiegel said in an advance report due for publication on Monday that the consignment, destined for China, was marked as raw materials but in fact contained dangerous chemicals.

It said these included six tonnes of wood preservative from the north German state of Lower Saxony and 34 tonnes of a substance used to treat the outer shell of military tanks which had passed its expiry date.
The consignment was due to be shipped to China via Croatia, but Croatian authorities refused to let it cross the border and sent it back to Hungary.

Last week Lebanon said it would ask Bonn to take back 680 tonnes of plastic waste which it said were contaminated with laboratory chemicals, pesticides and chemical fertilisers and had been shipped to Beirut illegally by two German companies.

German authorities said they were investigating the matter but had no evidence the consignment contained anything other than its declared contents of waste plastic granulate, which is not hazardous and needs no special export clearance.
